'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Taliban insurgency]]
**[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
***The [[Taliban]] captures [[Aybak, Samangan|Samangan]] (Aibak), the [[Provinces of Afghanistan|provincial]] capital of [[Samangan Province]], making it the sixth capture of a provincial capital by the [[Islamist]] group in the past four days. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/9/taliban-captures-sixth-afghanistan-provincial-capital-official (Al Jazeera)]
***The [[Afghan National Security Forces]] launch a [[counter-offensive]], in an attempt to retake [[Kunduz]], which was captured by the Taliban yesterday. Heavy fighting is reported elsewhere in the northern part of the country, where the Islamist group has launched an [[offensive (military)|offensive]]. Civilians flee Kunduz, trying to reach [[Kabul]] as there are conflicting reports as to who is responsible for dozens of civilian casualties. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/afghan-forces-battling-retake-kunduz-taliban-advance-north-2021-08-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[17 October Revolution]]
**Violence occurs in [[Lebanon]] due to the severe fuel shortages that are affecting the country, leaving three people dead. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/8/9/lebanons-worsening-fuel-crisis-sparks-violence-leaving-3-dead (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Algeria wildfires]]
**Seven people are killed and two others are injured by [[wildfire]]s in [[Tizi Ouzou Province]], [[Algeria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/10/algeria-forest-fires (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] begins to require people who want to enter shopping centres, cafés, restaurants, or travel by long-distance bus, train, and airplane, to show a [[Immunity passport#COVID-19 vaccination certificates|health pass]] generated by a [[QR code]], which contains either proof of full [[COVID-19 vaccination in France|vaccination]], a negative [[COVID-19 testing|test]] result from the previous 72 hours, or that the person has recovered from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210809-france-to-implement-coronavirus-health-pass-despite-protests (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Switzerland]]
****[[Swissmedic]] approves the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 12 and 17. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/second-anti-covid-vaccine-for-swiss-teenagers-approved/46853984 (Swissinfo)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]] 
*****[[Scotland]] moves to level zero and removes most of the remaining COVID-19-related restrictions, allowing all hospitality venues, including nightclubs, to reopen at full capacity and to remove most legal [[social distancing]] requirements. However, [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face masks]] remains mandatory in indoor public settings and on public transport, and must be worn by pupils and teachers at school for the first six weeks of the semester. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-58136277 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****[[Brunei]] reports a record 42 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours after reporting their first local infections in 15 months, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 406. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/brunei-sees-record-covid-19-cases-after-first-local-infections-15-months-2021-08-09/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 40,808 new cases and 588 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4.199 million and the nationwide death toll to 94,603. [https://english.aawsat.com/home/article/3123026/iran-says-one-person-dying-covid-19-every-two-minutes (Asharq Al-Aswat)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] begins administering second doses of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] dose for nearly 1.4 million elderly people following a months-long delay due to [[India]] suspending exports of vaccines due to a substantial increase in the number of cases there. The vaccines were donated by [[Japan]] and [[Bhutan]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/nepal-s-elderly-get-second-covid-19-vaccine-shots-after-months-long-wait (Radio France Internationale)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
*****The [[Therapeutic Goods Administration]] grants provisional approval for the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]], becoming the fourth vaccine to be approved for use in [[Australia]]. [https://www.smh.com.au/politics/federal/moderna-vaccine-gets-provisional-approval-in-australia-20210809-p58h9p.html (''The Sydney Morning Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Palau]]
****[[Palau]] reaches [[herd immunity]] as 80% of its 12-and-over population are vaccinated against COVID-19. Plans to vaccinate teenagers are underway as tourism reopens in the country. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/448816/palau-settles-into-new-normal-after-it-claims-herd-immunity (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[United States Secretary of Defense]] [[Lloyd Austin]] announces that all [[United States Armed Forces|service members]] will be required to be vaccinated by mid-September. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/pentagon-require-mandatory-covid-vaccines-mid-september-source/story?id=79314193 (ABC News)]
****The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|U.S. CDC]] announces that 60% of Americans have received their first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/nearly-60-americans-least-partially-vaccinated-against-covid-19-cdc-2021-08-09/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Arkansas]]
****[[Arkansas]] reports 103 hospitalizations from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record. [https://apnews.com/article/health-arkansas-coronavirus-pandemic-7ed21edba1069f6c57e07c42540021fe (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Egypt]]
***[[Egypt]] receives their first shipment of 261,000 doses of the single-dose [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.egyptindependent.com/egypt-receives-261600-doses-of-johnson-johnson-vaccine/ (''Egypt Independent'')]
*[[Guinea]] reports [[West Africa]]'s first death from the [[Marburg virus]] after a person died from [[viral hemorrhagic fever]]. [https://apnews.com/article/africa-health-united-nations-west-africa-guinea-1a530847edcb353184a3f46520787dc1 (AP)] 

'''International relations'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[Canada–United States relations]]
**[[Canada]] reopens [[Canada–United States border|their border]] to Americans and [[Permanent residency in Canada|permanent residents]] who are fully vaccinated against COVID-19 for non-essential travel. All travellers must present a negative [[COVID-19 test]] result from the previous 72 hours in order to enter the country. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/canada-reopens-its-border-for-fully-vaccinated-u-s-visitors-01628544473 (MarketWatch)]
*[[Foreign relations of Nicaragua]]
**[[Nicaragua]] recalls its ambassadors to [[Argentina]], [[Mexico]], [[Costa Rica]] and [[Colombia]] for "consultations" after those countries recalled their ambassadors to Nicaragua over a crackdown on the opposition in Nicaragua. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/nicaragua-recalls-mexico-argentina-colombia-costa-rica-ambassadors-2021-08-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[Egypt–Russia relations]]
**Direct commercial flights between [[Russia]] and [[Egypt]] resume for the first time since the [[Metrojet Flight 9268]] bombing in 2015, which killed 224 people, most of whom were Russian tourists. A [[Rossiya Airlines]] passenger plane landed in [[Sharm El Sheikh]] carrying 518 passengers, and was welcomed with a water cannon salute, [[rose]]s and flags. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/russian-flights-return-egypts-resorts-six-years-after-crash-2021-08-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Gretchen Whitmer kidnapping plot]]
**Federal prosecutors say that five men who were accused of plotting to kidnap [[Governor of Michigan|Michigan Governor]] [[Gretchen Whitmer]] also discussed [[Governor of Ohio|Ohio Governor]] [[Mike DeWine]] as a potential target. [https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2021/08/09/accused-whitmer-plotters-mulled-attacking-ohio-gov-dewine-feds-say/5544873001/ (''Detroit News'')]
*A priest is murdered at a church in [[Saint-Laurent-sur-Sèvre]], [[France]], by the same person who committed the arson at the [[Nantes Cathedral]] in July 2020. He is arrested after confessing to the killing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-58145468 (BBC News)]
*A barely legible letter to [[Pope Francis]] regarding the Vatican's financial scandals, which contained three bullets and is believed to have originated from France, is intercepted by postal workers in [[Peschiera Borromeo]], near [[Milan]]. The letter is being treated by authorities as a possible death threat against Francis. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/envelope-containing-three-bullets-sent-to-pope-francis/ar-AAN6oGB?ocid=BingNewsSearch (''Newsweek'' via MSN)] [https://www.euronews.com/2021/08/09/letter-sent-to-pope-containing-bullets-intercepted-by-postal-workers (Euronews)] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro]]
**The [[Government of Brazil|Brazilian government]] announces that [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] will attend a military parade featuring tanks and armored vehicles in [[Brasília]] tomorrow, as a preparation for military exercises. The parade is expected to pass near the [[National Congress of Brazil|National Congress]] building as a controversial bill reinstating paper ballots and ending [[Electronic voting in Brazil|electronic voting]], which is supported by the government, is set to be voted. As the bill is widely expected not to pass, critics argue that Bolsonaro is using the parade as a show of force and intimidation against the Congress. [https://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/politica/2021/08/amp/4942554-em-demonstracao-de-forca-bolsonaro-recebera-desfile-de-tanques-na-esplanada.html (''Correio Braziliense'')] [https://noticias.uol.com.br/colunas/thais-oyama/2021/08/09/bolsonaro-dara-demonstracao-de-forca-com-desfile-de-tanques-de-guerra.htm (UOL)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Climate change in the Arctic]]; [[2021 Russian wildfires]]
**Smoke from [[wildfire]]s in [[Siberia]] is detected in the [[North Pole|Geographic North Pole]] for the first time in recorded history, according to [[NASA]]. The [[space agency]] says that as of August 6 "most of Russia" is covered in smoke, while Russia's weather monitoring institute Rosgidromet says that the situation "continues to deteriorate" in the far-eastern [[Sakha Republic|Sakha]] region with around 3.4 million hectares (8.4 million acres) of land currently on fire. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/aug/09/smoke-siberia-wildfires-reaches-north-pole-historic-first (''The Guardian'')]
